messages.text:
Great! I moved the Geant4 material tracks to the storage folder in the top level directory, which has now the the older reference files and the newer one with less service material.



Also PR #112 got merged with a color schema:

- what I need now is: material_mapping for the new baseline 



Two stacked plots Geant4: 

- old baseline (beampipe, pixel, short strips, long strips - the detectors split in sensitive and passive, the latter shown by 50% opaque)
- new baseline (same colors)



Both plots should show the reconstruction/ACTS material as black markers and a ratio to the total Geant4 underneath, best using `unrooted` - the new baseline should also show a dotted line representing the old baseline (for total and short strip material) to illustrate the saving from the new readout scheme and reduced services.

I’ll identify the old and new recordings in `storage`, check the merged color scheme, and build the new ACTS material map. Then I’ll produce the two stacked comparisons with ACTS markers and ratio panels, using `unrooted` where it supports the required plotting.

The Spack registry still reports stale setup fingerprints and unverified full sources; I’ll recheck the actual runtime before running mapping. I’ll also verify the recording’s geometry identity: changing readout pitch alone does not remove physical material, so the savings comparison needs to identify which service changes the new file contains.

I found a provenance mismatch: the new file’s metrics point to the PR #109 compact, before PR #110’s reduced-service geometry. I’ll preserve both supplied files, use the 2 mm file as an intermediate control, and generate a separate current-baseline scan for the reduced-service comparison. The old and current baselines also differ in pixel layout, so I’ll distinguish the total change from the short-strip change.

The current-baseline scan is running successfully with the persistent `beamOn()` fix. I’m using the common range −4 < η < 4 for both plots, with the PR #112 colors and 50% opacity for passive material. The fresh geometry export for ACTS mapping is also underway.

The fresh scan completed: 100,000 geantinos, with one Geant4 run initialization and no aborts. ACTS mapping is now processing those tracks. I’m also checking the Geant4 component assignment and budget closure before drawing the sensitive/passive stacks.

The first checks found a boundary issue near some thin endcap cooling tubes: Geant4 records zero-length titanium crossings, and a few nearby steps disagree with the TGeo material lookup. I’m checking the affected material budget and whether ACTS drops only zero-length steps before accepting the map and plots.

ACTS accounts for the step-count difference exactly: it omits 185 zero-length slabs, with no loss of nonzero slabs or material budget on any ray. I’m now checking the remaining TGeo discrepancies against Geant4’s own geometry to resolve the component assignment.

The new ACTS map passes conservation and reload checks. The supplied PR #109 scan and the fresh scan also use exactly the same 100,000 rays: the full short-strip redesign reduces their mean radiation-length budget by 10.4%. That comparison includes the module, cooling and service changes; it does not isolate cables alone.

Geant4 resolves all 149 disputed steps to passive graphite pickup pieces, matching the recorded material. TGeo finds titanium at those same positions. I’ll retain that discrepancy in the report and use the audited Geant4 assignment for these steps. The 100,000-ray ACTS validation has also completed.

The comparison code now covers both radiation and interaction lengths, with a ratio panel beneath each. I’m finishing the audited component checks and figure rendering. The report will distinguish the total old-to-new baseline change from the PR #109-to-current redesign change.

The audited classification passes with no unassigned steps or unresolved material mismatches, and the figures are rendering. Over the common η range, the new baseline has 7.2% less total radiation-length material and 27.7% less short-strip material. Its total interaction-length budget is 2.9% higher, with the changed pixel baseline contributing to that increase.

Both figures are rendered and visually checked. I’m packaging the map, plots and reproduction commands, and arranging a separate review of the final numerical evidence. The report retains the Geant4/TGeo conversion issue and the map’s azimuthal-averaging and material-locality limits.

The map and fresh tracks are saved in `storage/nodd-tracker-des043-current`; both supplied files are unchanged. The separate review found one wording correction: I’ll label the old sample simply “validation rays,” since its original recording seed is unknown. This does not change the numerical results.
Really nice, but remove the old short strip dotted line from the new base-line, only keep the old-style Geant4 total
I’ll remove the old short-strip dotted line and keep the old Geant4 total on the new-baseline plot.
The revised PNG, PDF and SVG now keep only the dotted old Geant4 total. I’ve checked the updated figure visually, and all 17 checks pass. I’m finishing the review record.

Updated: the new-baseline plot now keeps only the dotted old Geant4 total. PNG, PDF and SVG regenerated; all 17 checks pass.
